Merra pulls her blanket-of-reeds closer and answers in a whisper.

"I couldn't see much from the cellar, only hear. Before you woke they brought the rider's horse round to the yard, and I heard Harl say 'Master Gaunt' like a man swallowing a stone. line: I pull the prayer wheel out of my pouch and turn it over in my scarred hands, staring at it as if I'd never really seen it. "This? I've spun it a thousand times, Mother. Show me how it's the key, and tell me what's sealed down there and why the founders didn't just destroy it."

entries.text: recall
fight: Fight over after 8 round(s). 48 seconds of fighting; now Day 2, 12:55:06 PM.
sheet: condition removed: prone

A quick out-of-character note first. The tracker was showing a fight in round 8 with "Breach Bandits" and Harl, you prone, one javelin and one ration fewer than I had recorded. Nothing in our play matches that, so I've treated it as a stale entry: I closed the fight and cleared the Prone condition. If you remember something I missed, tell me and I'll correct it. Your kit is otherwise as the sheet says (3 javelins, 8 rations).

Back in the lamplit nave, the priestess takes the prayer wheel from your palm and turns it so the lantern catches the rim.

"Look closer, child. You spun it a thousand times and never once pulled it." She presses her thumbnail into a seam at the hub, and the little brass drum twists a quarter turn with a click. The outer ring slides free. Inside, where you always assumed there was only a rolled scrap of prayer, lies a toothed bronze blade the length of your thumb, worn smooth, its notches cut in a pattern that matches nothing you know.

"That is half of the key. The other half hangs at my throat." She draws a matching blade from beneath her collar. "The crypt door answers only when both turn together, and only to someone of the temple's blood or oath. It was built so that no single keeper could be bribed or broken alone."

You ask what's sealed down there, and why it wasn't simply destroyed. She is quiet for a while. "The founders called it the Hollow King. I know little more than that. Not a corpse, not quite a spirit: a thing that fed on those who swore oaths to it, and could not be killed by any hand that tried. They bound it instead, and made the temple the lock. Destroying it, the old writings say, would have loosed whatever it had devoured." She closes your fingers around the bronze. "I think Gaunt wants it to answer to him. And I think he already knows the tithes were only to find out who would stand and who would run."

It's about 1 PM. You're at 8 of 15 HP and spent, and the baker's sons are riding for Merra. What does Grukka do?

entries.text: notebook: updated Old Crypt

A DM's note first: the sheet showed a fight in progress with "Breach Bandits," Harl, and you prone, plus one javelin and one ration fewer than I had recorded. None of that happened in the story I've told. The temple door is barred and the nave is quiet. I've cleared the stray fight and the prone condition. If you believe you spent a javelin or a ration, tell me and I'll correct the sheet.

Back to the nave. The old priestess takes the wheel from your hands and turns it slowly in the lamplight. It's a plain thing of blackened brass, no bigger than a fist, worn smooth by years of your thumb.

"Every child in this temple was given one," she says. "Yours is the only one with a spindle of iron instead of wood. Feel the weight." She presses a thumbnail into a seam in the cap you never noticed, and the cap turns with a small click. Inside, a slender iron rod no longer than your finger slides free, its end cut in a pattern of notches. From beneath her collar she draws a cord with a second rod on it, twin to the first but with the notches cut the other way. "Two halves. The crypt's lock accepts nothing else. And the prayer you've spun since you could walk is the word that sets them. The founders chose it because no thief would think to ask a child's toy."

She sets the rods together and they meet with a note like a struck bell. "As for what's sealed: it's a warden, child. Something old and bound that the founders found when they built here. They could not destroy it. It cannot be killed, only kept. They tried, and the first temple burned for it. So they built another on top, and set a key into the hands of whoever kept the faith, and they taught us to keep the door shut. Every priestess has done so. I don't know what Gaunt wants it for. I only know that he does, and that he has spent months and gold finding out which of us holds the key."

She presses the iron rod back into your palm and closes your fingers over it. "I'm old, Grukka. If he takes me, you hold it. Do you understand?"

You're at 8 of 15 HP, it's about 1 PM, and Tomas and Wil are on the east road for Merra. What does Grukka do?

input.add_to_description: The priestess's account: the founders sealed in a bound thing, a "hungering" that could not be killed, only kept. The prayer wheel's inner drum bears a hidden ring of seven small glyphs; the priestess's half is a bronze rod that fits its spindle. Together, turned in the right prayer, they open the crypt door. entries.text: notebook: updated Old Crypt

A quick note out of character: the tracker was showing a leftover fight (Harl and two "Breach Bandits") that doesn't match what we've played, so I've cleared it and the Prone condition. You're at 8/15 HP in the quiet temple, and I can't account for one javelin and one ration the sheet now shows missing, so tell me if that looks wrong.

The priestess takes the wheel from your hands and turns it so the lamplight falls on the brass drum. "Seven small glyphs, worn smooth by your thumbs. You thought they were decoration." She draws from her sleeve a short bronze rod, no longer than a finger, with a notched end. "This fits the spindle. Turn the wheel in the Seventh Prayer with the rod seated, and the crypt door opens. Neither half does anything alone."

"Below us is no god and no demon," she says. "The founders called it the Hungering: a thing that eats the strength of whatever stands near it and grows by it. They couldn't kill it. Every blade and blessing they tried only fed it. So they bound it, sealed it, and split the key between two keepers who would never share a roof. Destroy either half and the binding fails. That's why they didn't simply break it."

Her eyes find yours. "I gave you the wheel at five years old because nobody would look for a key in a child's hands. Gaunt knows now. He asked for anyone who'd defend this temple because he was hunting the other keeper, and last night he found you."

She lays the rod in your palm beside the wheel, and it is warm. "Merra will be brought home. But Gaunt will not wait long. Will you carry both halves, or shall I hide them again?" The bell above is silent now. What does Grukka do?
